newsitem.title: PERU: Spain's Mapfre to expand new Latam units.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Mapfre to expand new Latam units.

text.p: With Spain's largest insurer Corporacion Mapfre Cia Internacional de Reaseguros SA at the end of its Latin American tour of expansion, the company said Tuesday it was ready to start expanding its acquired units.
"Our objective now is vertical expansion. This means expansion of the companies we have invested in," Mapfre's secretary general Alberto Manzano Martos told Reuters.
Mapfre has been picking up stakes in insurance companies in over 10 Latin American countries, including Mexico, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Venezuela and recently Peru.
Mapfre is culminating a roughly $450 million expansion program to strengthen its overseas position, with 95 percent of this going to the Latin American market.
"With all our investments we have now completed our program of international horizontal expansion with the aim of being present in all the important Latin American countries," Manzano added.
It is now one of the largest insurers in Latin America and controls approximately 11 percent of the region's insurance market, according to company figures.

The company said it was keen to increase its presence in the life insurance market, which means setting up new subsidiaries of the recently acquired companies in Latin America, particularly in Mexico and Colombia. "We will set up subsidiaries of the new companies, like in Mexico which could deal with life insurance if that does not already exist in the company," Manzano added, stressing the neeed to strengthen the companies it has stakes in to fend off increasing competition.
"The main competition for us in the future will come from banks entering the insurance sector and for us the big competition will come from the Spanish banks," he added.
Mapfre's general secretary did not rule out further expansion in Latin America but said it would all depend on the success of the recent acquisitions.

Its last remaining acquisition in Latin America is in El Salvador, which is still to be completed. Its most recent puchase, a 51 percent stake in Peru's insurer El Sol Nacional for $8.5 million, was to strengthen its position in Peru. El Sol has a 5.4 percent stake in the domestic market.

Manzano welcomed the end of Peru's recent hostage crisis, where 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels held 72 VIPs in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima for 126 days before being crushed last week.
"If the economic and political stability of the government continues it will produce a phenomenon in a couple of years which will increase Peru's economic strength," Manzano said.

"This is a positive factor and will strengthen confidence in Peru," added El Sol Nacional's marketing manager Manuel Espinoza. He said Mapfre's priority in Peru is to expand the car insurance and life insurance sectors.
Sales for El Sol Nacional grew 18 percent year-on-year in 1996 and are exected to grow by 20 percent in 1997.
Spain's Mapfre posted net attibutable profit of 9.74 billion pesetas in 1996 versus 9.57 billion the previous year.
Mapfre's recent acquisitions include a majority stake in Venezuelan insurer Seguros La Seguridad for $35 million, and a stake in Chile's Euroamerica Seguros Generales SA.
It also control's Brazil's Vera Cruz Seguradora SA, which Mapfre said it bought for almost $60 million.
Mapfre is present in 27 countries, employs over 14,000 people in 2,972 offices and specializes in insurance, assistance, banking and finance and real estate.
